chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Muhammad ibn al-Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who divorced his wife, then he died while she was in her waiting period: she inherits him. And if she died while in her waiting period, he inherits her. And each of them inherits from the blood-money (diyah) of the other, provided that one did not kill the other.

And Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah added: 'And she observes the waiting period of the one who died, her husband.' Hasan ibn Sama'ah said: 'This statement was omitted from the book of Ibn al-Ziyad, and I do not think except that it was indeed narrated.'

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a divorced couple if one spouse dies during the waiting period?
ai.summary: This ruling by Imam Ali (AS) clarifies that the revocable divorce (Taliq) status persists until the expiration of the waiting period, thereby preserving full inheritance rights upon death. It further establishes the principle of reciprocal blood-money (diyah) between spouses, a nuance highlighted by Shaykh al-Tusi through the variant reading of Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, which emphasizes the widow's continued observance of the husband's iddah. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the precise moment when a divorced marriage contract is considered fully dissolved for inheritance purposes.
